title: UAPI stability: DO_KDF _pad check after ikm_fd extraction
description: ioctl_do_kdf in crypto2dev_fd.c checks op._pad[] for zeros (memchr_inv at line 1882) AFTER it has already extracted IKM bytes from the ikm_fd KEY fd (fget, mutex_lock, memcpy at lines 1844-1879). If ikm_fd != -1 and _pad is nonzero, the kernel has already: allocated ikm_buf, opened the KEY fd, locked it, copied IKM bytes out of the key object, and released the lock — all before the -EINVAL is returned. The IKM bytes are freed/zeroed at out_early (correct), so there is no information leak or memory leak. But it is a sequencing defect: the entire purpose of the _pad check is to reject calls with garbage reserved fields before doing any work. A _pad check that fires after sensitive key material has been speculatively copied does not serve that purpose. Fix: move the memchr_inv(_pad) check to immediately after copy_from_user and the string null-termination, before any fget or ikm_fd logic.
